transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 10:30 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Aurora Quants Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Infra), Diego Ramos (Quant Analyst), Fiona Chen (CFO - last 10m)

Summary (auto-gen maybe): discussion focused on unit economics for hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments; batching and KV/prefix caching levers; pilot and benchmark next steps; security/compliance questions.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll do a short intro then jump into cost economics - hosted vs dedicated vs private and what levers you folks have, yeah.
[00:18] Maya: hi thanks, we want to understand the per-token costs but also the operational tradeoffs, right - our main question is - can we hit our budget while keeping p99 latency under 300ms for shorter queries.
[00:30] Priya: got it. quick qual question - what's your current query profile? variant lengths? batchable?
[00:38] Diego: majority are short - 16 to 128 tokens, about 60% under 64, but we have a tail with long backtests ~ up to 1,200 tokens for model explainability. total volume ~ 30k tokens/day currently but plan to scale to 300k in six months.
[00:55] Liam: infra-wise we're on GCP, have a VPC, we prefer VPC peering for Private or dedicated and want KMS integration for keys. SOC2 is required.
[01:08] Jordan: great - that already pushes the conversation toward either Hosted for quick start or Dedicated/Private for predictability and data isolation. for cost math, typical per-token hosted pricing is X (we'll send the sheet) but the levers you can use are batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization (model variants).
[01:30] Priya: right and just to clarify - batching reduces unit GPU overhead by grouping inference across requests, but can increase tail latency. Redwood's smart batching tries to respect latency SLOs. also KV cache/prefix caching can dramatically cut repeated prefix token costs for chatty workloads.
[01:48] Maya: for our usage, we have a lot of repeated prompts and shared prefixes in the quant pipelines, so KV cache could be big. ballpark - how much improvement?
[01:58] Priya: from past pilots, caching can cut per-token billable compute by 20-70% depending on reuse - in a scenario like yours with repeating preambles you'd likely see 35-50% effective drop in tokens billed to the model. caveats: depends on prompt variability and caching window.
[02:16] Diego: and batching - how do you set the batching windows? we can't tolerate p99 spikes in the strategy UI.
[02:23] Sam: batching policies are configurable - target latency, max batch size, and prioritized routing; Redwood will auto-fallback to smaller batches during spikes to keep p99 within configured SLOs. there's also a dedicated pool option where you can pick throughput target and Redwood dedicates nodes so batching is more consistent.
[02:42] Fiona (joined): hi sorry, I'm on - quick note from finance, we need deterministic monthly cost for forecasting, we dislike per-token volatility.
[02:51] Jordan: totally - that's exactly where Dedicated (reserved capacity) helps - you commit to a pool (e.g., 4xA100 or Ampere configs) and get guaranteed throughput plus blended unit cost; plus we can model fixed monthly cost vs variable hosted spend.
[03:08] Maya: what's the delta between hosted per-token and dedicated unit cost? give me something concrete, like 1M tokens/day - what does hosted vs dedicated look like?
[03:16] Priya: ok quick rough example - hosted generation for an open 7B-ish model might be $0.0004 /k token equivalent (this is illustrative), with batching and cache you could lower effective cost to ~$0.00025; a dedicated pool with 4xA100 amortized could bring your effective unit cost to ~$0.00012-$0.00018 depending on utilization and quantization. we'll send a spreadsheet with line items - GPU amortization, infra egress, caching effects.
[03:40] Liam: can you clarify quantization impact - we already run 4-bit in internal experiments, how does Redwood support that?
[03:46] Priya: Redwood supports multiple quantization profiles; we can serve int8/4-bit model builds and surface recommended profiles per workload. quantization can reduce GPU memory and increase throughput - that lowers per-token cost. tradeoffs are some quality delta; we run eval sets to recommend profiles.
[04:05] Diego: how do we measure quality regressions? we need to ensure our strategy signals don't degrade.
[04:09] Sam: you'll get eval hooks and quality monitoring in Redwood Optimize - can tie regression alerts to prompt sets, and we can run automated A/B tests during rollout to compare outputs between baseline and quantized variants.
[04:21] Maya: security - SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO. can you provide attestations?
[04:26] Jordan: yes, Hosted has SOC2 and we integrate with customer KMS for dedicated/private; Private on-prem includes options for HSM. we'll share the security pack with SOC2 report, encryption whitepaper, and available pen test evidence.
[04:40] Liam: network-wise for Private we need either a package that runs inside our VPC or on-prem air-gapped option; what's the ops burden?
[04:48] Priya: Private deployment can be delivered as a customer-managed control plane with Redwood agents. ops burden depends on chosen mode - we provide a helm chart and support; typical small ops lift to manage upgrades and monitoring, but it's designed for enterprise teams with dedicated infra. Dedicated (hosted but reserved) is lower ops because Redwood manages infra.
[05:05] Diego: latency targets - we need p50 ~80ms, p99 <300ms for short queries. is that realistic on hosted?
[05:12] Priya: for short queries, hosted across curated low-latency regions and optimized kernels can hit those numbers on 7B and some 13B models, but p99 depends on region and queuing under high burst; Dedicated offers more predictable p99. also KV cache helps because repeated prefixes avoid re-compute.
[05:29] Maya: what about fallback policies - if dedicated pool is saturated, do you auto-failover to hosted?
[05:34] Jordan: yes, smart routing supports policy-based fallback: e.g., route to Dedicated first, if queue > threshold route to hosted or to a lower-cost quantized variant. you can define cost vs latency priorities.
[05:46] Fiona: finance question - how do you bill for KV cache savings? is billing based on tokens after cache or before?
[05:53] Priya: billing is on effective tokens executed on the model - so cached prefixes usually aren't billed as full model tokens. we account for cache hits and only charge for served tokens; logs show hit-rate so you can reconcile.
[06:05] Diego: any minimums for Dedicated? or commitment terms?
[06:09] Jordan: typical reserved capacity commitments start at 3 months for smaller pools and annual for enterprise discounts; we can do a 30-day pilot in many cases. pricing depends on pool size.
[06:19] Maya: sample pilot - we want to run a 2-week pilot on dedicated with our prompt set and compare to hosted. what do you need from us?
[06:25] Priya: we'll need sample prompts, typical concurrency, and a secure way to run the benchmark - we can do a controlled benchmark in our staging or spin up a dedicated test pool under a pilot contract. also need your SLA targets and the telemetry you want captured.
[06:38] Liam: network access - we can provide VPC peering or temporary SSH/jumpbox for the pilot, but we'd prefer peering.
[06:44] Sam: ok we'll include network runbook; Priya will own scheduling the benchmark.
[06:49] Jordan: back to unit economics, two more levers to remember: pre-warming/burst capacity and model selection - using a smaller, faster model for short queries vs a larger model for long context can significantly lower cost.
[07:00] Maya: do you support hybrid routing by model size? e.g., route short queries to a 7B and long context to 13B?
[07:05] Priya: yes - routing policies can direct requests by route, by header, or by detected length. you can also use an ensemble approach (cheap model + fallback to larger model on low-confidence).
[07:15] Diego: ensemble seems interesting - any data on false positive fallback cost?
[07:19] Priya: depends on fallback frequency; if fallback is rare it can be cheaper. we recommend calibrating confidence thresholds on historical data. we'll help with analysis.
[07:28] Maya: one more on billing - do you give token-line-item granularity per environment so we can allocate to product teams?
[07:34] Jordan: yes - Redwood Console has token-level breakdowns by API key, model, route, and team. billing export is granular for chargeback.
[07:43] Fiona: cost predictability is key for us - can you provide a blended cost model for forecasting?
[07:48] Jordan: yes - we'll provide a sample blended model: fixed reserved cost amortized across expected utilization + variable hosted overage. we'll model three scenarios (low/medium/high) and show per-token blended cost.
[07:59] Maya: what's typical hit rate for KV caching in production? you said 35-50% for repeats - seems optimistic.
[08:05] Priya: it's workload dependent; chatty support apps often see 50-70% for system prompts and common prefixes; quant workflows with templated prompts often sit in the 30-50% range. worst case it can be low if every prompt is unique.
[08:20] Diego: we do a lot of synthetic prompt generation so reuse might be moderate. we'll share our sample distribution.
[08:26] Maya: on the security docs - send SOC2, encryption, KMS integration details. also want to know retention policy options (30/90/never store).
[08:35] Jordan: Hosted defaults to ephemeral storage; enterprise can opt into longer retention for auditing but by default we support no retention for sensitive workloads. Dedicated/Private gives you more control; we'll include retention and deletion policies in the security pack.
[08:50] Liam: what logs are available for audits? full request/response or redacted?
[08:55] Priya: audit logs include metadata and token counts; request/response payloads can be disabled or redacted. we also support field-level redaction and KMS encryption of stored artifacts.
[09:06] Diego: operationally, who owns model upgrades and patching in Private?
[09:10] Sam: in Private (customer-managed) you own the underlying infra and upgrades; Redwood provides supported releases and upgrade scripts. in Dedicated (Redwood-managed), we handle upgrades during maintenance windows.
[09:21] Maya: ok next steps recap?
[09:24] Jordan: recap: Jordan will send hosted vs dedicated pricing spreadsheet with blended examples and three scenarios (low/med/high). Priya will schedule the dedicated pilot/benchmark and share the runbook. Maya will share sample prompt set and distribution. Liam will provide networking and security contacts. we'll aim to reconvene after initial benchmark results.
[09:42] Fiona: and finance will review the blended forecast once we get the spreadsheet.
[09:46] Maya: timeline - can we aim to kick off pilot next week?
[09:49] Priya: yes, if we get prompts and peering info today or tomorrow we can spin up the test pool early next week.
[09:55] Jordan: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up via email with the security pack, pricing sheet, and the pilot runbook.
[10:00] END
